dedupe_keys.name: port of nagoya ransomware attack on the terminal operating system july 2023

description: An account of the July 2023 ransomware attack that stopped container operations at the Port of Nagoya, Japan's largest port by cargo, drawn from the security firm Dragos and trade press. Coverage: the port's container terminals and their shared terminal system. Event: the port suspended operations after ransomware disrupted its systems on 4 and 5 July 2023, so imports and exports could not be processed; Japanese media reported LockBit 3.0 as the ransomware. According to the Nagoya Harbor Transportation Association, one cargo terminal resumed on the afternoon of 6 July with others later that day. Toyota said new car shipments were not affected, but loading and unloading of parts was, and it suspended a packaging line for export components. Format and access: free web articles; no official incident report was read. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: details come from secondary sources, and some operator details in the vendor analysis could not be checked. Useful for resilience and emergency response models of ports where a single terminal system is a common point of failure for many terminals and downstream supply chains. It relates to the Singapore cyber landscape report in the catalogue.
